description: Full Soridormi skill universe for Open Duck Mini v2. Skills are declared up front, but execution lands one-by-one through status and implementation phases. This manifest does not grant hardware execution.

strategy.notes: A skill may be declared even when unavailable. Status, actuator requirements, and phase determine whether it can be executed.

capability_groups.goal: Declare full skill universe and validate manifest.
CLI/runtime listing, status filters, and schema validation.
Expose existing policy velocity skills through safe wrappers.
Implement head/neck social gestures in MuJoCo.
Trajectory tracking and obstacle-aware clearance via evaluation and residual/RL.
Resolve world goals into bounded local route segments before any locomotion controller runs.
Fast walk/run after speed tracking is proven.
Arm/hand gestures only if matching hardware exists.

skills.description: Hold a stable standing posture with zero velocity command.
Cancel active locomotion and command zero velocity.
Track a bounded body velocity command vx, vy, and yaw.
Human-facing wrapper for natural requests like walk forward, walk slowly, and walk quickly. The speed label is lowered to a bounded positive vx command.
skills.notes: Executable semantic wrapper for Chromie and human-facing task planners. Use walk_forward(speed=slow|normal|medium|quick|fast_limited) for ordinary speech. It lowers to walk_velocity(vx>0, vy=0, yaw=0). True running remains future and should use run only after a validated controller exists.

skills.description: Human-facing wrapper for walk_velocity with small negative vx.
skills.notes: Keep conservative until backward commands are accepted in MuJoCo evaluation.

skills.description: Rotate left or right with near-zero forward velocity.
Human-facing wrapper for positive-yaw turn_in_place.
skills.notes: Wrapper should lower to turn_in_place(yaw>0).

skills.description: Human-facing wrapper for negative-yaw turn_in_place.
skills.notes: Wrapper should lower to turn_in_place(yaw<0).

skills.description: Walk forward while tracking a yaw command.
Human-facing wrapper for forward walk with positive yaw.
Human-facing wrapper for forward walk with negative yaw.
Track a small lateral velocity command.
Human-facing wrapper for positive lateral sidestep.
Human-facing wrapper for negative lateral sidestep.
Follow a short body-frame trajectory composed of velocity or waypoint segments.
skills.notes: This is the correct target for interactive movement: not merely survive, but follow the requested trajectory.

skills.description: Move toward a resolved world target by sensing, localizing, routing, planning short local trajectory segments, and executing only bounded locomotion skills. This skill must refuse raw natural-language goals such as 'the house' until a trusted target resolver supplies structured target and route data.
skills.notes: This is the missing bridge between Chromie language goals and Soridormi body control. Chromie may say the user asked for a house, but Soridormi must only receive a structured navigation goal with target pose/bearing, confidence, route segments, and local safety context.

skills.description: Track trajectory while lifting swing foot to clear a detected or specified obstacle.
skills.notes: BC will copy the teacher. Improvement beyond teacher should use residual/RL with terrain features and clearance reward.

skills.description: Maintain trajectory progress on low rough terrain.
Fast locomotion beyond current walking envelope.
skills.notes: Declared for roadmap only. Not executable until fast-walk/run policy is proven in MuJoCo.

skills.description: Transition from stable standing to sitting/rest pose.
skills.notes: Do not learn from walking-only teacher. Needs scripted pose/keyframe teacher, separate teacher policy, or future RL.

skills.description: Transition from sitting/rest pose to stable standing.
skills.notes: Do not learn from walking-only teacher. Needs scripted pose/keyframe teacher, separate teacher policy, or future RL.

skills.description: Lower the body height while maintaining balance.
skills.notes: Do not learn from walking-only teacher. Needs scripted pose/keyframe teacher, separate teacher policy, or future RL.

skills.description: Recover from a safe fallen/crouched pose to standing.
skills.notes: Do not learn from walking-only teacher. Needs scripted pose/keyframe teacher, separate teacher policy, or future RL.

skills.description: Small corrective recovery after disturbance without a full fall.
skills.notes: Do not learn from walking-only teacher. Needs scripted pose/keyframe teacher, separate teacher policy, or future RL.

skills.description: Slowly return supported head/neck joints to the neutral straight-ahead pose using a scripted MuJoCo trajectory.
skills.notes: This is the explicit fallback/home command for scripted head social skills; it should preserve non-head actuator controls while homing only head_neck joints.

skills.description: Turn head/neck toward a specified yaw/pitch direction using a scripted MuJoCo keyframe plan.

Turn head toward a structured person target direction provided by an external planner/perception layer and, by default, hold gaze on that target. Soridormi does not run perception here; it only executes bounded yaw/pitch offsets.
skills.notes: This implementation consumes structured target_yaw_rad/target_pitch_rad only. It uses the default gaze behavior to hold_target so the robot does not immediately return to neutral after looking at somebody. It does not run camera perception, person detection, raw natural language parsing, arms, hands, torso, or hardware. Concurrent locomotion overlays use a stricter bounded yaw/pitch and velocity envelope declared in concurrency.locomotion_envelope.

skills.description: Continuously track a person with head/neck while body remains safe.
Blink the simulated social eyes by toggling Soridormi visual-expression geoms. This is simulator-only and does not add motors or policy actions.
skills.notes: This implementation is visual-only in MuJoCo. It toggles open/closed eye geoms generated by soridormi_sim.social_eye_scene and never modifies the low-level locomotion policy, actuator list, arms, hands, torso, or hardware.

skills.description: Visible repeated bounded head pitch motion for yes/acknowledgement using scripted MuJoCo keyframes.
Visible repeated bounded head yaw motion for no/decline using scripted MuJoCo keyframes.
Gentle head/neck-only bow gesture using a neutral-home scripted MuJoCo trajectory. No torso or leg bow is attempted.
skills.notes: This implementation is intentionally head/neck only. Whole-body torso bow remains future work until posture control is validated.

skills.description: Composite social behavior for greeting a person.
skills.notes: Speech/TTS belongs outside Soridormi, for example Chromie. Soridormi only owns the body movement.

skills.description: Small head-only attention/listening gesture using a bounded neutral-home MuJoCo trajectory.
skills.notes: This implementation is a subtle listening/attention cue. It does not use perception, speech, arms, hands, torso, or hardware.

skills.description: Arm/hand wave greeting. Current Open Duck Mini v2 actuator map has no arm/hand actuators, so this is a future hardware-extension skill.
skills.notes: Declared so higher-level planners know the desired behavior exists conceptually, but Soridormi must reject it on the current robot.

skills.description: Point toward an object or direction. Requires arm/hand hardware not present in the current actuator map.
skills.notes: Declared so higher-level planners know the desired behavior exists conceptually, but Soridormi must reject it on the current robot.

skills.description: Interactive arm/hand contact gesture. Requires future arm/hand hardware and contact safety.
skills.notes: Declared so higher-level planners know the desired behavior exists conceptually, but Soridormi must reject it on the current robot.

body.primary_motion.description: Exclusive primary locomotion or whole-body control objective.

body.head_pose.description: Bounded head/neck pose overlay composed into the final body motor command.

visual.eyes.description: Independent visual eye-expression output that does not write motor commands.
